item.title: Throttling Starlink Is a Disaster for Ukraine and the United States
item.description: In demonstrating its unreliability as a security partner, the United States is eroding allied trust in U.S. defense and technology suppliers and in NATO.

item.title: Sustaining South Africa’s Progress in the Next Phase of the HIV Fight
item.description: South Africa has 8 million people living with HIV, and the government has introduced lenacapavir, a new HIV prevention drug. Thousands have started on the injections, but questions about future costs and supplies will need to be resolved to ensure the campaign’s success.

item.title: Risk to Refugee Return
item.description: This installment of Charting the Middle East highlights how the scale of unexploded ordnance (UXO) contamination, relative to returning populations, varies across Syria.

item.title: The AI Force the United States Needs is a Cyber Force
item.description: Cyberspace is the only warfighting domain without a dedicated service, and President Trump's calls for an AI Force won't fix that. A Cyber Force will.

item.title: Beyond the U.S.-China Binary: The New Landscape of AI Partnerships in the Global South
item.description: Global South countries are gaining new choices in building their AI ecosystems as China, India, and the Gulf States expand their technology offerings, creating new challenges for U.S. leadership.

item.title: Not Just an Island: Why Geography Should Not Drive U.S. Taiwan Policy
item.description: Taiwan’s geographic position in Asia’s first island chain should not become the main reason why the United States supports Taiwan’s security. The main focus of U.S. policy should be preventing a PRC attack on Taiwan and the regional and global catastrophe it would cause.
